title: A pointwise flat complete-intersection fibre admits a standard affine model
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ be any affine open neighbourhood of $s$. Assume that $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], that the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and that the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(s)$ in the local-ring sense specified in [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion]. Then there are an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ of $x$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, integers $n,c\geq0$, and polynomials $h_1,\ldots,h_c\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ such that the ring map induced by $f|_U:U\to V$ identifies $B$ with $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ as an $R$-algebra, and this presentation is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. In particular its nonzero fibre rings have Krull dimension $n-c$, as required by that definition.

source.place: Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic), implication (3) to (2), with standard syntomic written as its relative-global-complete-intersection affine presentation. The displayed fibre local ring is the canonical identification used immediately afterward in lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres.

proof.text: By finite presentation at x choose affine neighbourhoods U_0=Spec(A) of x and V_0 of s with f(U_0) contained in V_0 and A finitely presented over O_S(V_0). The restricted morphism f_0:U_0 -> S is locally of finite presentation: for every point y of U_0 the very same affine pair U_0,V_0 witnesses finite presentation at y in the cited definition. Choose an affine neighbourhood U=Spec(B) of x inside the open U_0 intersect f^{-1}(V), using the affine-open basis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to f_0, the affine open U of U_0, and the prescribed affine open V=Spec(R) of S. It gives that R -> B is finitely presented. Thus x belongs to U and f(U) is contained in V, without asserting that an open principal in V is principal in V_0.

source.place: Definition Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation) and Lemma Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) => (2); affine neighbourhood chosen using Schemes Tag 01IT.

proof.text: Let q be the prime of B corresponding to x and p=q∩R, corresponding to s. The local rings of the affine opens identify R_p with O_{S,s} and B_q with O_{X,x}; restricting a morphism to affine open neighbourhoods does not change these stalks. Hence the local map R_p -> B_q is flat by the assumed flatness at x.

source.place: Tag 01UE, condition (3), and Definition Tag 01U3 (flatness at a point), with the standard affine stalk identifications.

proof.text: Put F=B tensor_R kappa(p), a finite type kappa(p)-algebra since B is finitely presented over R. The affine fibre-product calculation identifies Spec(F) with the open of X_s induced by U. Its prime Q corresponding to x is the kernel of F -> kappa(q), and F_Q is canonically O_{X_s,x}. Consequently F_Q is a complete-intersection local ring over kappa(p) by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-ci-local-ring-principal-neighbourhood] to k=kappa(p), F, and Q. It gives h outside Q such that F_h is a global complete intersection over kappa(p). This is a criterion at the single prime Q; no assertion about other local rings of F is needed.

source.place: Tag 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime), (1) => (3); affine fibre identification as in Morphisms Tag 01UE and lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection] to the ring map R -> B, the prime q, and g=1. Its finite-presentation hypothesis is Step 1, its flat local-ring hypothesis is Step 2, and its fibre hypothesis is Step 3. We obtain an element g not in q, integers n,c, polynomials h_1,...,h_c in R[t_1,...,t_n], a relative global complete-intersection quotient T=R[t_1,...,t_n]/(h_1,...,h_c), and an R-algebra isomorphism B_g ≅ T. Since g is not in q, U\cap D(g)=Spec(B_g) is an affine neighbourhood of x, maps into V, and has the asserted presentation.

source.place: Tag 00SY, implication (3) to (2), applied to the affine coordinate map R -> B; the scheme-theoretic formulation is Morphisms Tag 01UE.

proof.text: For every prime of R whose fibre of T is nonzero, the definition of a relative global complete intersection gives Krull dimension n-c. This is exactly the final “in particular” clause.

source.place: Definition Tag 00SP (relative global complete intersection), fibre-dimension clause.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01UE, implication (3) => (2), with the affine refinement from Tag 01TQ, fibre-prime criterion Algebra Tag 00SG, and algebraic local model Algebra Tag 00SY.
